required_observations: The role-owned permission table is a foundational model that the relationship-based target explicitly rejects.
The released decision request, boolean response, tenant and resource identifiers, and continuous service remain compatibility obligations.
The stable gateway boundary can route tenant cohorts to an independently built engine without making the target import the legacy role model.
required_decisions: Build and verify a target-native relationship engine independently of the role table rather than evolving the rejected core in place.
Preserve the outer decision contract and transition tenant cohorts in stages through the gateway with comparison, stop signals, and an old-engine retirement condition.

Use the complete module for target-native core construction and the incremental module for staged transition, keeping implementation, traffic movement, policy-data movement, and retirement authority separate.
anti_findings: Do not choose direct or big-bang transition merely because the new core is built independently.
Do not evolve the role table into a union of role and relationship concepts that makes the target depend on the rejected model.
Do not classify staged rollout as evolve-in-place construction when the target core must be derived independently.
safety_requirements: Planning remains read-only and does not route traffic or mutate policy data.
Implementation, cohort cutover, data movement, and old-engine retirement each require their own authorization.
